page: Amazon Web Services c6i.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor. Running at a nominal frequency of 3.5 GHz, the configuration provides 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs via hyperthreading. Memory capacity is set at 96.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU). The CPU architecture incorporates 54 MB of shared L3 cache and supports specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA_NI for accelerated vector and cryptographic processing. The instance does not include local disk storage and connects to network-attached block devices, supported by a 19 Gbps baseline network throughput.

Benchmark results place the c6i.12xlarge solidly within middle-tier expectations across most general compute tasks, registering a PassMark CPU score of 47,897.3 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,737.0. It demonstrates distinct strength in cryptographic and visual computation, with PassMark CPU encryption (42,481.53) and Geekbench image processing (15,272.0) both ranking in the top 25%. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 165.37 GB/sec for reads and 68.06 GB/sec for writes. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O depends entirely on network storage channels over the baseline network fabric.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6i.12xlarge delivers high compute density without incurring costs for excess memory or idle local disks. This hardware profile is appropriate for compute-bound batch processing, CI/CD compilation (supported by a Geekbench clang compilation score of 37,048.0), static web serving (yielding 39.43 GB/sec throughput), and cryptographic processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c6i.12xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provisions 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs alongside 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It features hardware cryptographic acceleration (AES, SHA_NI) and AVX-512 with VNNI support, supported by a 54 MB L3 cache. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and network connectivity offers a 19 Gbps baseline. Performance testing reflects solid mid-tier multi-threaded processing with top-quartile performance in encryption and image processing tests. The instance is structured for compute-heavy workloads such as distributed compilation, batch processing, image and video processing pipelines, and static web serving where high core density is prioritized over expansive memory capacity.
